newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan shinkin firms to brief on merger - sources.
newsitem.headline: Japan shinkin firms to brief on merger - sources.

text.p: Two credit associations, known as shinkin banks in Japan, will hold a news conference at 3 p.m. (0600 GMT) on Friday on the issue of a merger, industry sources said.
The two are Chiba Shinkin Bank and Ryoso Shinyokinko, which are both based in Chiba Prefecture, near Tokyo, they said.
The credit associations are larger than credit unions but are not classified as "banks" under Japanese financial law.
They lend money mainly to members but take deposits widely. Most borrowers are small- and medium-sized businesses. Unlike credit unions, they are monitored by the Finance Ministry.

The sources said that the expected merger was aimed at helping Ryoso, which has had some financial woes over the past few years. the end of March 1996, the 58th largest among the 420 shinkin banks in Japan.
Ryoso"s deposits totalled 139.12 billion yen, ranking 191st on the list.
Chiba Shinkin and Ryoso officials declined to comment.
